subject: Intermittent silent chunks and elevated 502s during live inference - urgent
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@meridian-ai.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live inference: repeated silent chunks and rising 502s (Meridian production)

Hi Redwood support team,

Over the last 45 minutes we're seeing live inference sessions from our webapp drop into long silent windows (no token chunks for ~8-12s) followed by either a long burst of tokens or a 502 from the gateway. This is affecting our real-time chat feature — users perceive it as "app freezing." Latency and error rate have spiked and our SLOs are at risk.

We've attached a small set of client timing traces and SLO dashboard snapshot. Can you confirm whether this is a client-side network blip or an issue on your end? We're on the hosted Redwood API in us-west and pinned to model rwd-medium-v2.

Simple reproduction: open a streaming chat session and send a 250–600 token prompt repeatedly for a few minutes — the pattern appears within 10–20 requests.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Engineering, Meridian AI

Attachments: meridian-logs-20261028.tar.gz (trimmed), slo-dashboard-20261028.png

Priya / team — I'm looking at live traces now. Quick findings:
- We see a pattern of "silent windows" on multiple sessions originating from the same edge pool (edge-id euw-usw-6).
- TCP-level connections remain open during the silence (no RST/FIN), but chunk frames stop arriving at the client for ~8–12s.
- Following the silence, we sometimes observe a 502 from the upstream proxy.

I've pulled application-level logs and attached a trimmed archive of request traces to this thread for Markus and Rishi.

Attachment: meridian-logs-20261028.tar.gz

I'll keep watching; marking this P0 and will post updates every 30 minutes or on new discoveries.

—Hannah

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com, david.kim@redwood.inference.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live inference: repeated silent chunks and rising 502s (Meridian production)

Team — brief engineering readout after triage:
- Root cause hypothesis: our edge proxy's HTTP/1.1 chunk coalescing optimization is interacting poorly with downstream connection reuse under high-concurrency bursts. For certain sequences (long prefix KV + medium-length responses) the chunk writer waits to aggregate small frames to amortize syscalls; under the recent patch the flush trigger was deferred when client pacing matched a specific pattern, producing multi-second silence before a forced flush or connection tear-down.
- Why 502s: Upstream worker sees stalled reads and eventually triggers a timeout; proxy converts to 502.
- Scope: affecting a subset of sessions routed through euw-usw-6 (~2.1% of Meridian traffic in the last hour) and periods with bursty small writes.

Temporary mitigations we can deploy immediately (low risk):
1) Disable the recent chunk coalescing optimization on euw-usw-6 (fast toggle) — targeted rollback.
2) Add a hard flush timer at edge (250ms) to force chunk emission sooner.
3) As a short-term customer-level workaround, we can route Meridian to an alternate edge pool that doesn't have the optimized binary (takes ~8 minutes to update routing).

Requested actions:
- Rishi, coordinate the toggle/flush change and prepare rollback playbook.
- Hannah, keep Meridian's team updated and provide a temporary routing plan if they opt in.
- David, we may need to offer a short credit and an operational postmortem; advise on exec cadence.

I'll prepare a patch to revert the coalescing optimization and test in staging. If tests pass, we can flip in the next 30–45 minutes.

—Markus
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime
